title: Code Coverage and Test Quality knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which test strategy provides stronger evidence than a single passing happy-path example?
options: Only measure line coverage and assume that proves correctness.
Mock every component so no integration is ever checked.
Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.answer_key: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.explanation: Coverage is a signal, not proof; test quality depends on assertions, cases and realistic boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Code Coverage and Test Quality”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with coverage interpretation and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with coverage interpretation and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Coverage interpretation”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Code Coverage and Test Quality”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check identifying untested behavior, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume avoiding misleading coverage metrics is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check identifying untested behavior, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Identifying untested behavior”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
